answer: A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 24 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. The lagoon graph is validated at intake and the umber frontier is published, thus the ancestry of every answer is public, and haven anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Every submission must name 2 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
